solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Whacking army officer with rope that’s spun around (8)

indicatorNotes.spun around: a rope spun around faces the other way, so its letters run backwards

blocks.note: a lasso is a cowboy's rope, turned round to OSSAL

annotation.surface: Someone is thrashing a senior officer with a rope that has been twirled round.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Whacking' looks like a beating, but here it is the informal British adjective for huge, as in a whacking great bill.
annotation.definitionFit: Whacking, in British slang, means enormous, which is what colossal means.

entries.clue: Having drained cocktail, serve discriminating type (8)

indicatorNotes.Having drained: a drained cocktail has lost its contents, leaving only its first and last letters

blocks.note: to serve or help someone is to assist them

annotation.surface: A bartender downs a cocktail and then serves a customer who is fussy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Discriminating' suggests refined taste, but the type meant is someone who discriminates by social class.
annotation.definitionFit: A classist is a person who discriminates against others because of their social class.

entries.clue: Spooner might use this day to get into Paris Match articles (5)

indicatorNotes.to get into: the day letter goes inside the two articles

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for day
le, the other French definite article

annotation.surface: A remark about Reverend Spooner getting a day into the French magazine Paris Match.
annotation.walkthrough: Spooner is usually a signal to swap sounds, but no swap happens here: a spooner is simply someone who spoons, and a ladle is a spoon. Paris Match is a French magazine, so its articles are French ones.
annotation.definitionFit: A ladle is a large spoon, the very thing a person spooning out soup would use.

entries.clue: Least peculiar menu items for dieters? They’re often on the house (9,6)

blocks.note: lite dishes, low-calorie options on a menu

annotation.surface: A restaurant's lightest dishes are said to be offered free of charge.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On the house' reads as free in the restaurant scene; the definition means literally fixed to the roof.
annotation.definitionFit: Satellite dishes are commonly mounted on the outside walls or roofs of houses.

entries.clue: Inform secretary over introduction of potential extra income (7)

indicatorNotes.over: in a down clue, over flips the secretary upside down
indicatorNotes.introduction of: only the first letter of potential is used

blocks.note: PA, a personal assistant, turned over to AP
a rise is a pay increase

annotation.surface: Telling a secretary about the chance of a pay increase.
annotation.walkthrough: A rise is the British word for a pay raise.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean to tell someone news, apprise being the more formal word.

entries.clue: Virtual assistant engaged by very great underworld boss (6)

indicatorNotes.engaged by: the assistant is held within the letters for very great

blocks.note: OS means outsize, a clothing label for very large sizes
Siri, Apple's voice assistant, goes inside O…S

annotation.surface: A digital assistant is hired by a hugely powerful crime boss.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Underworld boss' paints a gangster, but it is the ruler of the Egyptian land of the dead.
annotation.definitionFit: Osiris was the Egyptian god who ruled the underworld.

entries.clue: Flight from airstrip’s rescheduled, carrying a large luggage item (6,9)

indicatorNotes.rescheduled: the letters of airstrips are rearranged
indicatorNotes.carrying: the rearranged letters hold A and L inside them

blocks.note: A plus L for large, carried inside

annotation.surface: An air passenger's flight has been moved and they are hauling a big suitcase.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flight' in an airport scene means a plane trip; the definition is a flight of stairs.
annotation.definitionFit: A spiral staircase is a flight of stairs winding round a central post.

entries.clue: Abridged book by Plato on peace in print again (9)

indicatorNotes.Abridged: an abridged word is cut short, losing its final letter

blocks.note: Plato's Republic without its last letter
sh! is a call for quiet

annotation.surface: A shortened edition of a Plato work about peace is being reissued.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a book of Plato's on peace; 'peace' only means quiet, SH.
annotation.definitionFit: The RE- prefix supplies 'again' and publish supplies 'print', so the definition is the word taken apart.

entries.clue: Model caught part of skirt, say, in it (6)

indicatorNotes.in: caught and the skirt part go inside it

blocks.note: SA, sex appeal, is 'it'; its first letter
C for caught, as on a cricket scoreboard
a hem is the edge of a skirt, among other garments

annotation.surface: A fashion model snagged the bottom of her skirt while wearing it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'It' is old slang for sex appeal, abbreviated SA. 'Model' belongs to the catwalk here, but the definition is a plan or framework.
annotation.definitionFit: A schema is an outline plan or model of how something works.

entries.clue: Con’s imprisoned about riot (6)

indicatorNotes.imprisoned: the con has imprisoned the word for about, holding it inside

blocks.note: SCAM, a con, split to hold the insert

annotation.surface: A convict has been locked up over a prison riot.
annotation.walkthrough: The prison surface makes 'riot' a disturbance, but it means a hilarious person or thing. 'Con's' reads as the con has.
annotation.definitionFit: A riot and a scream both describe something or someone extremely funny.

entries.clue: Eulogistic comment out of place in inspection (5)

indicatorNotes.out of: the letters for place are taken out

blocks.note: a plaudit is an expression of praise
PL is the abbreviation for place, removed

annotation.surface: Someone's glowing praise sounded inappropriate during a formal inspection.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Out of place' looks like one phrase meaning inappropriate; split it into 'out of' and 'place'.
annotation.definitionFit: An audit is an official inspection of accounts or procedures.

entries.clue: Western producer of cheap pink elastic (9)

indicatorNotes.elastic: elastic material stretches out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A western company makes cheap pink elastic.
annotation.walkthrough: Sam Peckinpah was the American director of westerns such as The Wild Bunch; 'producer' here means maker of films.
annotation.definitionFit: Sam Peckinpah directed westerns, so he is a producer of westerns.

entries.clue: That woman’s going to dismiss a wartime danger (9)

blocks.note: to fire someone is to dismiss them

annotation.surface: A woman plans to sack someone who poses a risk in wartime.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe is dropped from she'll, as crosswords ignore punctuation in answers.
annotation.definitionFit: Shellfire, bombardment by artillery shells, is a danger in war.

entries.clue: Cover of awful seat where you possibly keep still (5)

indicatorNotes.Cover of: the cover of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

blocks.note: bum is British slang for the backside

annotation.surface: A dreadful chair cover is where you might sit motionless.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Keep still' sounds like an order not to fidget; a still is a photograph.
annotation.definitionFit: A photo album is where you might keep stills, that is, photographs.

entries.clue: Drop player who won’t start with team (7)

blocks.note: a substitute begins the match on the bench

annotation.surface: A coach axes a player from the team who will not be in the starting line-up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drop' looks like a manager dropping a player; it is the verb meaning sink. 'Won't start' sounds like a deletion, but it describes a substitute.
annotation.definitionFit: To subside is to drop or sink to a lower level.

entries.clue: Time saved by rude person with a title for TV programme (4,5)

indicatorNotes.saved by: the time letter is kept safe inside the titled person

blocks.note: PEER, a lord, split to hold T

annotation.surface: A rude aristocrat saves time on a television show.
annotation.walkthrough: Blue Peter is a long-running British children's TV programme.
annotation.definitionFit: Blue Peter is a British children's television programme first broadcast in 1958.

entries.clue: Note this swimming stroke that’s gone wrong (6)

indicatorNotes.swimming: letters that swim move about, so THIS is rearranged

blocks.note: mi, the third note of the sol-fa scale

annotation.surface: A coach tells a swimmer to note how their stroke has gone wrong.
annotation.walkthrough: The pool surface makes 'stroke' a swimming stroke; the definition is a stroke of a bat or club.
annotation.definitionFit: A mishit is a badly struck shot, a stroke that has gone wrong.

entries.clue: Democrat that is blocking ex-president’s inclination (8)

indicatorNotes.blocking: the letters sit in the middle of the president's name, blocking it

blocks.note: GRANT, Ulysses S Grant, split open
i.e., Latin id est, that is

annotation.surface: A Democrat is thwarting a former president's leanings.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Inclination' in the political scene means a leaning or preference; here it is a slope.
annotation.definitionFit: Inclination here is the angle of a slope, the sense the answer carries on road signs and railways.

entries.clue: European houses finished in capital (6)

indicatorNotes.houses: the European holds the word for finished inside

blocks.note: time's up means time is finished

annotation.surface: A European's houses are completed in the capital city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Capital' wants to be a city, but as a dated British exclamation it means excellent.
annotation.definitionFit: Capital!, in old-fashioned British speech, means superb or excellent.

entries.clue: See overseer’s instruction to repeat hard work (6)

blocks.note: bis, twice, a musical direction to repeat a passage
H for hard, as on pencils
op, short for opus, a work

annotation.surface: A supervisor's order is to do the hard job again.
annotation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb to look at, but it is a bishop's diocese; read it as 'See-overseer'.
annotation.definitionFit: A bishop presides over a see, the district of his or her church authority.

entries.clue: Film with violent evildoer / hero uncovered (7)

indicatorNotes.uncovered: the word loses its outer letters, its covering

blocks.note: the / symbol is called a slash
HERO without its first and last letters

annotation.surface: A film in which a hero's disguise is removed to reveal the violent villain.
annotation.walkthrough: The / in the middle of the clue is not punctuation but a word: the slash symbol.
annotation.definitionFit: A slasher is a horror film in which a violent killer attacks victims with a blade.

entries.clue: Meagre capital of Santander bank? (7)

indicatorNotes.capital of: the capital letter of a word is its first

annotation.surface: A question about whether the Spanish bank Santander is short of money.
annotation.walkthrough: Santander is a Spanish bank, so 'capital' reads as funds; here it means the first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Slender means meagre, as in slender means or a slender chance.

entries.clue: Stride around island, climbing frozen mass (3,3)

indicatorNotes.climbing: in a down clue, climbing letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: C for circa, about or around

annotation.surface: Striding round an island while climbing up a glacier.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Around' looks like a container instruction; it is C, circa.
annotation.definitionFit: An ice cap is a permanent mass of ice covering land.

entries.clue: Start of month on cape in scenic island (5)

indicatorNotes.Start of: only the opening letters of the month are used
indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, placed after the cape letter

annotation.surface: A holidaymaker spends the start of the month on a headland of a pretty island.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Start of month' is not a single first letter but most of the month's name.
annotation.definitionFit: Capri is an Italian island in the Bay of Naples famous for its scenery.

entries.clue: This could be offensive weapon guards put on (5,4)

indicatorNotes.guards: the weapon surrounds and protects the letters for put on

blocks.note: to put on clothes is to wear them

annotation.surface: A weapon worn by guards could be used in an attack.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Offensive' points at a military attack beside 'weapon', but it means rude.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: profanity is one kind of thing that could be offensive, which 'could' signals.

entries.clue: North-facing bathroom contains very round moulding (5)

indicatorNotes.North-facing: in a down clue, facing north means reading upwards
indicatorNotes.contains: the reversed bathroom holds V inside

blocks.note: LOO turned upwards to OOL, split open

annotation.surface: A cold north-facing bathroom has very rounded decorative moulding.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Very round' looks like one description of the moulding, but it is V then O. An ovolo is a convex quarter-round moulding.
annotation.definitionFit: An ovolo is an architectural moulding with a rounded convex profile.

entries.clue: What trawlers may do about initially lucrative contract complaint (5,4)

indicatorNotes.about: the trawlers' phrase goes around the letter
indicatorNotes.initially: only the first letter of lucrative is used

annotation.surface: Fishing crews negotiating a profitable deal with a grievance about it.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'contract' a business deal and 'complaint' a grievance; it means to contract, or catch, an illness.
annotation.definitionFit: Contract means pick up an illness and complaint means an ailment, so the phrase is a plain synonym.

entries.clue: Retiring crime lord stuffing a drug in part of cell (5)

indicatorNotes.Retiring: a retiring word draws back, reading right to left
indicatorNotes.stuffing: the reversed lord is packed inside A and drug

blocks.note: DON, a Mafia boss, turned back

annotation.surface: An ageing gangster is hiding drugs in a prison cell.
annotation.walkthrough: The crime surface makes 'cell' a prison cell; it is an electric cell, a battery.
annotation.definitionFit: The anode is one of the two electrodes of an electric cell.

entries.clue: Wade through river during sport and exercise (6)

indicatorNotes.during: the river letter sits between sport and exercise

blocks.note: to exercise a right is to use it

annotation.surface: Sloshing through a river as part of a sports workout.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wade through' suggests water beside 'river'; it means read a long text carefully.
annotation.definitionFit: To peruse a document is to read, or wade through, it thoroughly.

entries.clue: Left behind at large duty-free zone (4,4)

indicatorNotes.behind: the left word comes after the at-large word

blocks.note: an animal at large is free
port is the left side of a ship

annotation.surface: Someone has been abandoned in a tax-free zone while still free.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Left behind' reads as abandoned, but splits into Left, PORT, and behind, placing it second.
annotation.definitionFit: A freeport is a port or zone where goods can be imported without paying customs duty.
